img-gi-esoph.intro: Start with the normal esophagus on two axial CT levels, then the staging studies: EUS for T (and local nodes) and PET/CT for nodes and metastases.

plates.title: Normal CT: Upper Chest (Aortic Arch)
plates.caption: Contrast-enhanced axial CT at the aortic arch. Hashmi R, Sectional Anatomy Quiz II, Asia Ocean J Nucl Med Biol (PMC5765337), CC BY 3.0; letter labels removed.

hotspots.label: Esophagus
hotspots.blurb: Behind the trachea, slightly left. Upper thoracic tumors are here.

hotspots.label: Trachea
hotspots.blurb: Invasion = T4b; fistula risk.

hotspots.label: Aortic Arch
hotspots.blurb: T4b if invaded.

hotspots.label: Spinal Cord
hotspots.blurb: Keep Dmax ~45 Gy.

hotspots.label: Lungs
hotspots.blurb: Lung V20 <20% (esp. before esophagectomy) lowers pulmonary complications.

plates.title: Normal CT: Mid Chest (Left Atrium)
plates.caption: Contrast-enhanced axial CT through the left atrium, where the esophagus lies right behind it. Hashmi R, Sectional Anatomy Quiz IV, Asia Ocean J Nucl Med Biol (PMC6661304), CC BY 3.0; letter labels removed.

hotspots.label: Mid Esophagus
hotspots.blurb: Directly behind the left atrium.

hotspots.label: Left Atrium
hotspots.blurb: Heart is a key OAR: lower heart dose lowers cardiac toxicity.

hotspots.label: Descending Aorta
hotspots.blurb: Left of the esophagus.

hotspots.label: Azygos Vein
hotspots.blurb: Right of the esophagus.

hotspots.label: Subcarinal Nodes
hotspots.blurb: Common site of esophageal nodal spread.

plates.title: EUS: Esophageal Wall Layers
plates.caption: High-frequency EUS of a normal esophageal wall (left, red box) with a schematic of its nine echo layers (right). Standard EUS shows these as five layers. Yun SM et al., J Korean Soc Radiol 2024 (PMC11473974), Fig. 2, CC BY-NC 4.0.

hotspots.label: Mucosa (Layers 1–4)
hotspots.blurb: Tumor limited here = T1a: may be treated with endoscopic resection.

hotspots.label: Submucosa (Layer 5, Bright)
hotspots.blurb: Invasion = T1b: nodal risk rises, so surgery or chemoRT.

hotspots.label: Muscularis Propria (Layers 6–8)
hotspots.blurb: Invasion = T2.

hotspots.label: Adventitia (Layer 9)
hotspots.blurb: Through the wall = T3 (no serosa in the esophagus, so tumors spread early).

plates.title: PET/CT: Esophageal Cancer Staging
plates.caption: (A) Coronal CT and (B) FDG PET/CT of a mid-esophageal cancer (white arrows) with avid lesser-curvature nodes (yellow arrows) and a para-aortic node (arrowheads). Tashiro H et al., Surg Case Rep 2025 (PMC12702577), Fig. 1, CC BY 4.0.

hotspots.label: Mid-Esophageal Primary
hotspots.blurb: Avid tumor. Contour with CT, endoscopy, and PET together (PET helps define the length).

hotspots.label: Primary on PET
hotspots.blurb: The FDG-avid primary. PET/CT defines the length of the tumor for the GTV and screens for distant disease.

hotspots.label: Lesser Curvature (Perigastric) Nodes
hotspots.blurb: Regional node.

hotspots.label: Para-aortic Node
hotspots.blurb: An avid node near the aorta below the diaphragm. Para-aortic nodes are distant (M1) for esophageal cancer.

img-gi-stomach.intro: The GEJ and cardia at T11–T12, with the celiac axis and crura. This is the level for distal esophageal, GEJ, and proximal gastric tumors.

plates.title: Normal CT: GEJ / Upper Abdomen (T11–T12)
plates.caption: Contrast-enhanced axial CT at the gastroesophageal junction in a healthy adult. Häggström M, CT of a normal abdomen and pelvis (Wikimedia Commons), CC0.

hotspots.label: GEJ / Cardia
hotspots.blurb: Distal esophageal and GEJ adenocarcinomas.

hotspots.label: Liver
hotspots.blurb: Mean liver dose limits matter for distal esophagus and gastric fields.

hotspots.label: Spleen
hotspots.blurb: Near the gastric fundus and pancreatic tail.

hotspots.label: Diaphragmatic Crura
hotspots.blurb: Wrap the esophagus at the hiatus.

hotspots.label: Celiac Axis / Nodes
hotspots.blurb: Celiac nodes are regional for esophagus and stomach.

hotspots.label: Aorta
hotspots.blurb: Retroperitoneal landmark.

img-gi-pancreas.intro: The normal pancreatic head and its vessels first, then a pancreatic-protocol CT (thin-slice, arterial and portal venous phases), which decides resectability.

plates.title: Normal CT: Pancreatic Head (L1–L2)
plates.caption: Contrast-enhanced axial CT through the pancreatic head in a healthy adult. Häggström M, CT of a normal abdomen and pelvis (Wikimedia Commons), CC0.

hotspots.label: Pancreatic Head
hotspots.blurb: Tumor here causes the double duct sign.

hotspots.label: SMA
hotspots.blurb: Surrounded by a fat collar; loss of the fat plane suggests encasement.

hotspots.label: SMV
hotspots.blurb: To the right of the SMA.

hotspots.label: Duodenum
hotspots.blurb: SBRT OAR: limit hot spots to avoid bleeding/ulcer.

hotspots.label: Kidneys
hotspots.blurb: Keep both kidneys' dose low (e.g., V20 <30%).

hotspots.label: Stomach / Bowel
hotspots.blurb: Nearby hollow organs limit pancreatic doses.

hotspots.label: Aorta
hotspots.blurb: The SMA leaves the front of the aorta about 1 cm below the celiac axis and runs down behind the pancreatic neck.

plates.title: Pancreatic-Protocol CT (Portal Venous Phase)
plates.caption: Portal venous phase CT of a hypoenhancing pancreatic head mass (red arrow) abutting, but not deforming, the SMV. A stent is in the common bile duct. Louis M et al., Cureus 2025 (PMC11981547), Fig. 2, CC BY 4.0.

hotspots.label: Hypoenhancing Head Mass
hotspots.blurb: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma is dark (hypoattenuating) relative to normal pancreas.

hotspots.label: SMV Contact
hotspots.blurb: Venous contact with contour irregularity = borderline (if reconstructable).

hotspots.label: SMA with Fat Collar
hotspots.blurb: Preserved fat around the SMA = no arterial contact. Soft tissue >180° = locally advanced.

hotspots.label: CBD Stent
hotspots.blurb: Double duct sign with the dilated pancreatic duct.

hotspots.label: Aorta
hotspots.blurb: The SMA arises from the front of the aorta; follow it forward to judge arterial contact.

img-gi-liver.intro: HCC can be diagnosed on imaging alone in a cirrhotic liver. Know the enhancement pattern and the LI-RADS categories.

plates.title: Multiphase CT: Hepatocellular Carcinoma
plates.caption: Multiphase CT of HCC in segment 6: (A) arterial phase hyperenhancement, (B) washout on the delayed phase, with tumor extending into the right portal vein (second arrow). Han JE et al., J Liver Cancer 2021 (PMC10035689), Fig. 1A–B, CC BY-NC 4.0.

hotspots.label: Arterial Phase Hyperenhancement
hotspots.blurb: HCC is fed by the hepatic artery, so it lights up early.

hotspots.label: Washout (Delayed Phase)
hotspots.blurb: Becomes darker than liver later.

hotspots.label: Portal Vein Tumor Thrombus
hotspots.blurb: Enhancing thrombus expanding the vein: advanced HCC; SBRT can treat it.

hotspots.label: Spleen
hotspots.blurb: Portal hypertension.

img-gi-rectal.intro: High-resolution pelvic MRI is the single most important rectal cancer study: it decides T stage, the margin, and who needs neoadjuvant therapy.

plates.title: Axial T2 MRI: Mid Rectum
plates.caption: Axial T2 MRI of a T3 mid-rectal cancer reaching the left mesorectal fascia (a threatened margin). Pikūnienė I et al., Cureus 2023 (PMC10493462), Fig. 1a, CC BY 4.0; arrow removed.

hotspots.label: Rectal Tumor
hotspots.blurb: Note depth into the mesorectal fat (T3 substage).

hotspots.label: Mesorectal Fat
hotspots.blurb: Contains the mesorectal nodes.

hotspots.label: Mesorectal Fascia (Involved)
hotspots.blurb: Distance tumor-to-MRF: ≤1 mm = threatened.

hotspots.label: Anterior Organs (Seminal Vesicles / Vagina)
hotspots.blurb: Invasion = T4b.

hotspots.label: Bladder
hotspots.blurb: Bright on T2 because it is full of urine. Anterior to the seminal vesicles in men.

plates.title: Rectal MRI: Axial T2 (Perpendicular to the Tumor)
plates.caption: Axial T2 MRI of two rectal cancers, with the mesorectal fascia traced as a dotted line. (a) T3ab tumor with short extramural spread (arrows), MRF clear. (b) T3cd tumor reaching the MRF (arrowheads). Bogveradze N et al., Insights Imaging 2023 (PMC9849549), Fig. 1, CC BY 4.0.

hotspots.label: Tumor (Intermediate T2)
hotspots.blurb: Intermediate signal, brighter than muscle, darker than fat.

hotspots.label: Extramural Spread into Mesorectal Fat
hotspots.blurb: Depth beyond the muscularis: T3a <1 mm, T3b 1–5, T3c 5–15, T3d >15 mm.

hotspots.label: Mesorectal Fascia
hotspots.blurb: Thin dark line. Tumor, node, or EMVI ≤1 mm from it = threatened CRM.

hotspots.label: Tumor Reaching the MRF (MRF+)
hotspots.blurb: Tumor within 1 mm of the mesorectal fascia means a threatened margin: this pushes the patient toward TNT and makes a negative TME margin harder.

plates.title: Rectal MRI: EMVI, Tumor Deposits, and Nodes

hotspots.label: EMVI (Tumor in a Vein)
hotspots.blurb: Tumor signal expanding an extramural vein: higher risk of distant metastasis.

hotspots.label: EMVI (Coronal View)
hotspots.blurb: On the coronal image the tumor signal grows along an enlarged mesorectal vein that stays attached to the primary.

hotspots.label: Tumor Deposit
hotspots.blurb: Irregular tumor nodule that follows the course of a vein but is separate from the primary. Counted as N1c and a high-risk feature.

hotspots.label: Suspicious Mesorectal Node
hotspots.blurb: Irregular border, heterogeneous signal, or round shape (size alone is unreliable).

plates.caption: T2 MRI of a low rectal cancer in three planes: (A) coronal and (B) axial EMVI (red arrows), (C) tumor deposits (green) versus a malignant node (blue). Curcean S et al., Cancers 2024 (PMC11394290), Fig. 2, CC BY 4.0.

plates.title: Rectal MRI: Sagittal T2
plates.caption: Sagittal T2 MRI of a high rectal cancer (m, bracket) 10 cm from the anal verge (*), touching the anterior peritoneal reflection (red arrowhead). Natout M et al., Diagnostics 2025 (PMC11989207), Fig. 3a, CC BY 4.0.

hotspots.label: Lower Tumor Edge
hotspots.blurb: Measure the distance to the anal verge: low tumors (<5 cm) are candidates for organ preservation strategies.

hotspots.label: Anorectal Junction
hotspots.blurb: Tumor reaching the sphincters or puborectalis may need an APR.

hotspots.label: Peritoneal Reflection
hotspots.blurb: Tumors above it invading peritoneum = T4a.

hotspots.label: Prostate / Seminal Vesicles (or Vagina)
hotspots.blurb: Invasion = T4b.

hotspots.label: Sacrum / Presacral Space
hotspots.blurb: Presacral nodes; tumor here complicates resection.

img-gi-anal.intro: The normal anal canal and groins on CT, then PET/CT, which is especially good at finding inguinal and pelvic nodes.

plates.title: Normal CT: Anal Canal & Groins
plates.caption: Contrast-enhanced axial CT at the top of the anal canal in a healthy adult male. Häggström M, CT of a normal abdomen and pelvis (Wikimedia Commons), CC0.

hotspots.label: Anal Canal
hotspots.blurb: Anal SCC target.

hotspots.label: Sphincter Complex
hotspots.blurb: Internal and external sphincters.

hotspots.label: Ischioanal Fossa
hotspots.blurb: Fat lateral to the sphincters; tumor can spread here.

hotspots.label: Inguinal Nodes / Femoral Vessels
hotspots.blurb: Always in the anal cancer field (and for low rectal tumors invading the anal canal).

hotspots.label: Femoral Heads
hotspots.blurb: OAR in groin fields.

hotspots.label: External Genitalia
hotspots.blurb: OAR in anal cancer IMRT (skin reaction).

plates.title: PET/CT: Anal Cancer
plates.caption: Axial fused FDG PET/CT of anal cancer: (a) small primary in the anal canal, (b) avid right inguinal node, (c) right distal external iliac node. Koppula BR et al., Cancers 2022 (PMC9179927), Fig. 39, CC BY 4.0.

hotspots.label: Anal Canal Primary
hotspots.blurb: Size sets T stage (2 cm and 5 cm cutoffs).

hotspots.label: Inguinal Node
hotspots.blurb: Regional (N1a). Gets a higher dose (50.4–54 Gy) when involved.

hotspots.label: External Iliac Node
hotspots.blurb: Regional (N1b).

hotspots.label: Bladder (Physiologic)
hotspots.blurb: Excreted FDG.

gallery.title: PET/CT: inguinal node
gallery.caption: FDG-avid inguinal (yellow), external iliac (red), and lateral pelvic (dotted) nodes in anal cancer. Park IJ, Chang G, Ann Coloproctol 2020 (PMC7837391), Fig. 2A–B, CC BY-NC 4.0.

gallery.title: RTOG anorectal atlas
gallery.caption: Elective nodal CTV (yellow) per RTOG guidance on axial CT slices for anal cancer, from L5 down to the inguinal nodes. Dapper H et al., BMC Cancer 2019 (PMC6664500), Fig. 1, CC BY 4.0.
